Subject: Integrating Cortex SaaS with AWS Marketplace metering

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again — Cortex is excited to finalize the Marketplace listing. We’ve got two implementation questions before legal and finance will sign off: 1) confirm the entitlement flow for per-seat + compute usage (we surface both a seat count and per-token/second compute meter), and 2) where should Cortex deliver the fulfillment payload (SaaS entitlement webhook vs. AWS fulfillment URL)?

Attached is our SOW draft and a short spec on the meter format. Can Redwood map the billing signals (seat + compute) to a single Marketplace entitlement key? If not, what’s your recommended approach so we don’t double-bill customers?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Alex Park
Head of Product Ops, Cortex Analytics
attachments: Cortex_SOW_draft.docx (docx), SaaS_Metering_Spec_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <ops@cortex.ai>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integrating Cortex SaaS with AWS Marketplace metering

Hi Alex — great to meet you over email. I put together a short checklist and next steps below to keep legal and procurement happy and to unblock engineering: 

- Entitlement model: Redwood recommends using a primary entitlement per-customer (Marketplace entitlement ID) with additional usage dimensions attributed via metering records (dimension: compute_seconds, dimension: seat_count). This prevents duplicate entitlement grants while enabling per-dimension pricing.
- Fulfillment endpoint: we support both SaaS entitlement webhooks (preferred for immediate activation) and AWS fulfillment S3/URL patterns. For Cortex I recommend SaaS webhook to reduce sync lag.
- Contract path: Redwood will generate a DocuSign agreement for the Marketplace SaaS contract (we’ll include the fulfillment URL and entitlement mapping appendix).
- Tasks & owners: 
  * Redwood: generate metering spec mapping (SoO) — owner: Marcus Lin — due 2026-01-19
  * Cortex: confirm pricing matrix & seat logic — owner: Alex Park — due 2026-01-18
  * Redwood Legal + Cortex Legal: finalize Marketplace addendum — coordinate via DocuSign link

I’m looping in Kimberly from Revenue Ops for procurement sequencing. Can we target go-live the week of Feb 2 if Cortex signs this week?

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Partner Sales (Marketplace), Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | soojin.lee@redwood.ai
From: AWS Marketplace Support <aws-marketplace-support@amazon.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cortex.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Integrating Cortex SaaS with AWS Marketplace metering

Hello Soojin and Alex,

Thanks for the details. A few items from our side to confirm: 
1) You can map multiple usage dimensions to a single SaaS entitlement. The entitlement grant is a single identifier; metering records can include dimensions (dimension 1=seat, dimension 2=compute_seconds). Our billing will aggregate according to the dimensions you register in the metering plan.
2) For immediate activation we recommend the SaaS fulfillment webhook pattern. Ensure the fulfillment response contains the entitlementId and effectiveTimestamp.
3) DocuSign: please use the public DocuSign integration (we will accept the marketplace addendum template). We will need the AWS-signed addendum returned within 3 business days of DocuSign completion for co-sell eligibility.

Best,
Priya Shah
AWS Marketplace Partner Support
